title: Sports journalist Rick Westhead wins Balsillie prize for book about hockey culture in Canada
summary: Veteran sports journalist Rick Westhead's book that takes a deep dive into hockey culture in Canada has won the $70,000 Balsillie Prize for Public Policy.

image.caption: Sports jurnalist Rick Westhead won the Balsillie Prize for Public Policy Tuesday for his book looking at hockey culture in Canada, We Breed Lions: Confronting Canada's Troubled Hockey Culture. (Rick Westhead/Penguin Random House Canada/Handouts/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Veteran sports journalist Rick Westhead's book that takes a deep dive into hockey culture in Canada has won the $70,000 Balsillie Prize for Public Policy.
We Breed Lions: Confronting Canada's Troubled Hockey Culture explores sexual assault, hazing and abuse
The Writers' Trust of Canada announced We Breed Lions: Confronting Canada's Troubled Hockey Culture as the winner of the prize at a private dinner in Toronto on Tuesday evening.
Westhead's book explores hockey's reckoning with allegations of sexual assault, hazing and abuse that rocked the sport in recent years.
Westhead investigates inside dressing rooms while also looking ahead to a more hopeful future by profiling individuals and organizations committed to educating players.
Jurors praised Westhead for confronting Canadian hockey culture with "clarity, rigorous evidence and unflinching purpose."

blocks.text: The annual award, which is in its sixth year, recognizes non-fiction books that advance policy discussions on social, political, economic and cultural topics that matter to Canadians.
The prize is funded by the Balsillie Family Foundation as part of a $3-million commitment to support Canadian literature through the Writers' Trust.

The runners-up received $7,500 apiece. They included Dennis Molinaro Under Assault: Interference and Espionage in China's Secret War Against Canada; Moira Welsh for The Astonishing Lives of Older Women: How to Create Pleasure Over Peril in Peak Longevity; Jesse Winter for Wild Fire: Dispatches from a Country Ablaze and Tim Wu for The Age of Extraction: How Tech Platforms Conquered the Economy and Threaten Our Future Prosperity.
